title: One sign exception is needed for 91 selected worm responses, but stricter samples permit cell signs
abstract: We tested whether separate source and target cell signs explain mean response signs on anatomical links in C. elegans. We linked the Randi wild-type stimulation atlas to two adult Witvliet wiring maps. At q below 0.05 and at least three occurrences, 91 selected chemical-linked responses required exactly one pair-specific sign exception. An eight-edge negative-product cycle and a feasible fit proved this minimum without relying on an optimizer bound. A uniform additive mean-response change of 0.041506 delta F/F was necessary and sufficient to permit the model with zero responses allowed. Requiring chemical links in both adults, at least five occurrences, or q below 0.01 removed the conflict. The both-adult role graph had no cycles and could not test this model. No measured response-error bound was available. Different animals, pooled responses, sparse constraints and indirect propagation prevent a biological sign-rule claim. Code, exact certificates, source hashes, evidence tables and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact minimum sign exceptions and uniform additive response-change bounds in seven overlapping selections. Zero exception counts show model feasibility, not a biological mechanism. The primary conflict does not survive stricter occurrence or q thresholds.
